newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-PISTONS' HILL AND DUMARS LEAD PISTONS PAST PORTLAND.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-PISTONS' HILL AND DUMARS LEAD PISTONS PAST PORTLAND.

text.p: Grant Hill scored 27 points and Joe Dumars converted eight free throws in the final 45 seconds to seal a 98-89 victory for the Detroit Pistons over the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday.

Terry Mills' basket gave Detroit its biggest lead of the game at 90-74 with 4:22 remaining before Chris Dudley netted five points in a 9-0 Portland run that closed the gap to 90-83 with 62 seconds to go.
Rookie Marcus Brown completed a rare four-point play with 33 seconds left to cut it to 94-89, but Dumars continued to make his free throws and ensured Detroit's fourth consecutive win.

In Charlotte, Reggie Miller poured in a season-high 40 points as the Indiana Pacers snapped a three-game skid and earned a split of a home-and-home series with a 106-95 victory over the Charlotte Hornets.
Rik Smits added 22 points and 11 rebounds, while Travis Best had 11 points and 11 assists for Indiana.
Glen Rice scored 34 points and rookie Malik Rose had 14 points and seven rebounds for Charlotte.

In Cleveland, Buck Williams, stepping in for the injured Patrick Ewing, scored eight of his 12 points in the fourth quarter as the New York Knicks rallied for a 75-65 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
Williams, who had missed the last three games due to the death of his father, manned the middle in place of Ewing, an All-Star who suffered a groin injury against Boston on Tuesday.
The Cavaliers went 8:43 without a field goal.
At Golden State, Gary Payton scored 10 of his 26 points in the first quarter as the Seattle SuperSonics raced to an 18-point lead and cruised to an 111-86 rout over the Golden State Warriors.
Payton, an Oakland native, hit six three-pointers.
Craig Ehlo, Detlef Schrempf and Hersey Hawkins had 14 points apiece for Seattle.

In Miami, Alonzo Mourning scored 10 of his 24 points in the first quarter as the Miami Heat grabbed an early lead and pulled away for a 103-83 victory over the undermanned Boston Celtics, who lost their seventh straight game.
Voshon Lenard scored 20 points and Tim Hardaway added 15 for the Heat.
David Wesley scored 23 points and Todd Day 19 for the Celtics, who trailed by as many as 24 points and fell to a league-worst 1-17 on the road.

In Orlando, Penny Hardaway scored 32 points and matched a season high with eight assists as the Orlando Magic made a trio of key three-pointers down the stretch on the way to a 112-105 victory over the Phoenix Suns.
Rony Seikaly had 18 points and 12 rebounds and Derek Strong added 18 and 11 for the Magic, who won for the eighth time in 10 games.
"We'll take this one tonight," Orlando coach Brian Hill said. "I still didn't think we were particularly sharp, especially offensively.

In Philadelphia, Jerry Stackhouse sank a transition 16-foot jumper from the right wing at the buzzer to lift the Philadelphia 76ers to their first home win in 13 games, a 101-99 thriller over the Toronto Raptors.
Rookie Allen Iverson scored 31 points, Don MacLean had 21 in 25 minutes and Clarence Weatherspoon had 17 and nine rebounds for Philadelphia.
Stoudamire scored 25 points and Marcus Camby had 18 points for the Raptors.

In San Antonio, Teenage rookie Kobe Bryant scored eight of his 19 points in a decisive fourth-quarter surge as the Los Angeles Lakers rallied for their fifth straight victory, 99-92 over the San Antonio Spurs.
Eddie Jones scored 23 points and fellow All-Star Shaquille O'Neal added 21 and 19 rebounds for the Lakers, who erased a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit.
Dominique Wilkins had 28 points and Sean Elliott 23 points for the Spurs.
